title: KV grain-splitting and hot/cold segmentation to reduce fragmentation in GPU KV cache
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Problem: KV cache fragmentation on GPUs increases effective memory pressure and leads to more frequent evictions, higher per-token cost, and degraded SLOs for long-context workloads. This ticket proposes a new allocation and mitigation strategy that reduces internal fragmentation by combining variable-grain allocations ("grain-splitting") with hot/cold segmentation and opportunistic coalescing during idle GPU cycles.
spec:
Overview:
- Introduce 'grain tiers' (e.g., 64B, 256B, 1KB, 4KB logical grains) rather than a single fixed slot size. Requests allocate the smallest grain tier that fits the KV entry to minimize internal wasted space.
- Track per-GPU hot/cold segments: frequently-accessed KV entries are placed in 'hot' pools that favor small-grain allocation and fast lookup; cold entries are grouped into block-backed segments for larger contiguous free ranges.
- Maintain lightweight per-stream freelists for immediate allocations to avoid global contention; background 'segment consolidator' merges adjacent free grains into larger free blocks in cold segments when the GPU has >10% idle time.
- Allocation hints from serving runtime: callers can pass 'expected-ttl' (short|medium|long) and 'avg-value-size' to bias allocation grain and segment. If no hint, use online estimator based on recent access patterns.
- Eviction policy: prefer evict-from-cold-first; when evicting in hot pool, try to coalesce freed grains immediately into per-stream transient free runs to serve upcoming allocations.
- Background compaction: on low-util windows, perform GPU-optimized memmove-style compaction within a segment to produce contiguous free ranges; limit compaction bandwidth to avoid interfering with latency-critical requests.
- Telemetry: expose per-GPU metrics: fragmentation_ratio, avg_internal_waste_per_entry, number_of_grains, compaction_throughput, compaction_time_percent, idle_compaction_events.
Implementation notes:
- Use device-side kernels for compaction where possible to avoid PCIe overhead. Fall back to host-driven copy for older GPU families.
- Safety: compaction runs must preserve KV handles and update index atomically; use double-buffering of indexes and lightweight fence protocol to avoid lost references.
- Backward compatibility: provide feature-flag gated rollout; default to older fixed-slot allocator until runtime confirms correctness metrics.
rollout_plan: 1) Prototype in dev cluster behind feature flag (2 weeks): implement grain tiers, freelists, and telemetry. 2) Canary on 5% of serving traffic with compaction disabled (1 week): validate allocation correctness and metrics. 3) Enable opportunistic compaction during known low-load windows on canary group (1 week). 4) Progressive rollout to 25%/50%/100% over two weeks while monitoring fragmentation_ratio and tail latency. 5) If fragmentation improves and tail latency stable, flip feature flag default for new hosts and ship migration tool for in-place upgrade.
risks_and_mitigation:
- Risk: compaction may increase latency if scheduled poorly. Mitigation: strict bandwidth caps, preemptible compaction, and latency-aware scheduler.
- Risk: allocator complexity introduces bugs (use-after-free or lost indexes). Mitigation: thorough unit/integration tests, canary rollout, and index double-buffering.
- Risk: some workloads may see worse locality if misclassified. Mitigation: runtime feedback loop that moves misclassified entries between hot/cold based on access heatmap.
metrics:
Success criteria (measurable):
- Reduce avg_internal_waste_per_entry by >= 35% for long-context workloads (measured over 24h).
- Reduce frequency of full-cache evictions by >= 20% at 95th percentile load.
- No more than 2% regression in 99th percentile request latency after enabling compaction (measured across canary hosts).
- Observability: fragmentation_ratio metric present and stable in Console dashboards with alerts when > 0.25.
acceptance_criteria:
- Implementation behind flag deployed to dev and passes correctness/unit tests.
- Canary verification: no safety/consistency incidents on canary (0 data corruption reports).
- Fragmentation metric improvement meets targets for at least three workloads (chat long-history, conversation reranking, long prompt code completions).
- Telemetry and dashboarding completed and alerts configured.
- Rollout runbook and rollback steps documented and reviewed by SRE.
